# How to read

Under each question there is a `- [ ] A:` line.

- **Tick it without writing anything:** you agree with the proposal.
- **Tick it and add a detail:** you agree, with that detail.
- **Leave it unticked and write:** I revise the proposal.

Built tonight (0.4.3) and open to change: the rail of tabs, the Calls, Devices,
Accounts and Agents tabs, and the fix for the username of a linked account. The Agents
tab is only a picture of what could come; nothing runs.

# 1. The rail of tabs

Five tabs (plus Agents) did not fit as words over a 290 px sidebar, so they became a
rail of icons on the far left (as in Discord or Slack), with Ctrl+1…6, an unread badge
on Chats, a green dot on Calls while a call or share runs, and our picture at the
bottom (opens the picture editor). The tab's name is the sidebar's title.

- [ ] A:

# 2. Agents: their own account, or a tab of their own?

Proposal: an agent is a Jami account of its own on this machine (not a linked device,
as D-18 says), created and deleted in the **Agents** tab, which stays a tab rather than
a section of Accounts: agents are things you talk to, accounts are who you are.

- [ ] A:

# 3. How an agent runs

Proposal, first version:

1. "new agent" asks for a name, a picture (the pixel editor) and a kind: Claude Code or
   Codex, both through ACP (Agent Client Protocol: the agent runs as a subprocess and
   speaks JSON-RPC over stdio).
2. Joma creates a Jami account for it (no username on the name server, unless you want
   one) and adds it as a contact of your accounts, so it shows in Chats like a person.
3. A message to the agent's conversation goes to its ACP session; its answers, tool
   calls and permission requests come back as messages. Permission requests become
   buttons (allow once, always, deny).
4. The agent runs only on this machine, in a working directory you choose, and only
   while Joma runs. Your other devices see the conversation (it is a normal Jami
   conversation) and can write to it: the machine running the agent answers.
5. Contacts can be given access to an agent later (it is a Jami account: they can add
   it), off by default.

- [ ] A:

# 4. What the agent may do

Proposal: the working directory is fixed per agent; the ACP permission prompts are
always shown to you (never auto-allowed at first); no screen or remote control for
agents until we discuss it again.

- [ ] A:

# 5. Logging in with another device and the username

What happened: you linked an account here, and Joma offered "choose a username". The
linked account did have one, but Joma read it only from details the daemon fills in
later. Since 0.4.3 Joma asks the name server for its own name once online, and the top
bar shows `@name` (verified in the nest: a fresh profile linked to `arol` shows
`@arol`, sees the three devices, and got the picture).

If you had typed another handle: the name server holds one name per account and names
cannot be taken back, so registering a second name for an account that has one fails
("already registered"); a name nobody has would have been tried and refused. Joma now
hides "choose a username" once the name is known.

Proposal: keep it this way; "choose a username" appears only when the name server says
the account has none.

- [ ] A:

# 6. Devices all called "zoma"

Every test profile on this machine named its device after the hostname, so the Devices
tab lists "zoma" three times. On real machines names differ, but two Joma on one machine
(or a renamed laptop) look the same. Proposal: a new device names itself
`<hostname> · Joma` and the Devices tab shows the first 8 characters of the id next to
equal names.

- [ ] A:
